column3: Talagrand's ultimate matching conjecture (Conjecture 5.8 of The Status of my favorite problems): for alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2 and a universal L, with probability tending to one as N grows, two independent samples X, Y of N i.i.d. uniform points of [0,1]^2 admit a matching pi with sum_i exp[(sqrt(N/log N)|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/L)^alpha_j] <= 2N for j=1,2; alpha=infinity means max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N/N). Research Problem 17.1.2 of Upper and Lower Bounds for Stochastic Processes (2nd ed., 2021) states it with Y evenly spread, a sufficient form by lem:two-sample-matching-transfer.

For N>=2, alpha in (0,infinity] and point sequences X,Y,Z of length N: if sigma_1 matches X to Z and sigma_2 matches Y to Z with sum_i exp[(sqrt N|P_i^j-Z^j|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha] <= 2N (or the maximum bound L sqrt(log N/N) at alpha=infinity), then sigma_2^-1 sigma_1 matches X to Y with the same bound at constant max(2,2^(1/alpha))L. Hence an evenly-spread matching theorem holding with probability 1-eps_N gives the two-sample one with probability 1-2eps_N, no independence of the samples assumed.

If a matching pi of point sequences satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N, N>=2, then max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N)(log 2N)^(1/alpha_j)/sqrt N, and for alpha_j>=1 the coordinate distances sum to at most 2L sqrt(N log N). At alpha_1=alpha_2=4 the Euclidean distances have sum <= 4L sqrt(N log N) and maximum <= 4L(log N)^(3/4)/sqrt N; at (2,infinity) Shor's two bounds hold with 2L.

For X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread, and any alpha_1, alpha_2 in (4,infinity] and L'>0, it is false that with probability tending to one some matching satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L' sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N (maximum bound at infinity) for j=1,2. So the diagonal exponent 4 of the ultimate matching conjecture cannot be raised in the evenly-spread setting.

For a separable cost C(z)=Psi_1(|z_1|)+Psi_2(|z_2|) with Psi_j convex, nondecreasing, finite, Psi_j(0)=0, and N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2 whose counts in every cell Q of a grid of side delta are at least lambda|Q|: for every h in (0,1/2), min over matchings of sum_i C(X_i-Y_pi(i)) is at most sup over Lipschitz g of [int g d(mu_X-mu_Y) - (1-2h) lambda int C*(grad g) dx] + 2hN(Psi_1(delta/h)+Psi_2(delta/h)), mu_X, mu_Y the cell-smeared measures and C* the convex conjugate (possibly infinite).

For alpha_1,alpha_2 in [1,infinity], L>=132, X i.i.d. uniform and Y evenly spread in [0,1]^2: if with probability tending to one D_N <= (L/2) sqrt(N log N), D_N the sup of int G d(mu_X-mu_Y) over Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) dx <= 2 on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N), psi_alpha(t)=e^(t^alpha)-1 and psi_infinity(t)=N(t-1)_+, then with probability tending to one a matching has sum_i exp[(|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/s)^alpha_j] <= 2N for finite alpha_j and max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= 2s for alpha_j=infinity; for two i.i.d. samples with constants doubled.

There is L>=132 such that for every alpha_1,alpha_2 in [2,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2, for X i.i.d. uniform and Y evenly spread in [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one every Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) dx <= 2 (psi_alpha(t)=e^(t^alpha)-1, psi_infinity(t)=N(t-1)_+) has cell-averaged discrepancy int G d(mu_X-mu_Y) <= (L/2) sqrt(N log N), on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N).

In the setting of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction (X i.i.d. uniform, Y evenly spread, L>=132, grid side about L sqrt(log N/N)/32), for exponents alpha_j in [1,infinity] with |1/alpha_1-1/alpha_2|<1/2, with probability tending to one the penalized discrepancy D_N is at least sqrt N (log N)^(3/4-(1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2)/2)/(4L_1), L_1 universal. So the bound (L/2) sqrt(N log N) fails for every L below the curve 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2, and on the curve away from its endpoints D_N >= sqrt(N log N)/(4L_1).

For a separable convex finite cost C with C(0)=0, N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2 smeared by probability measures within l-infinity distance delta_X, delta_Y of the points whose sums are absolutely continuous with densities at least lambda, h in (0,1/2), lambda'=(1-2h)lambda: for every bounded field Phi with int grad g . Phi = int g d(nu_X-nu_Y) for all Lipschitz g, the minimal matching cost is at most lambda' int C(Phi/lambda') dx + hN sum_(k=1,2) (Psi_k(delta_X/h)+Psi_k(delta_Y/h)).

For L>=260, X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread, with probability tending to one there is a matching with sum_i exp[N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|^2/(L^2 log N)] <= 2N for j=1,2: the conjecture's conclusion at the off-curve pair (2,2), coordinatewise.
If xi_1..xi_n are i.i.d., mean 0, variance sigma^2>0, |xi_i|<=c, S their sum, s=sigma sqrt n, x>=1, m=ceil(128x^2)<=n and c^2<=s^2/(2m), then P(S>=xs)>=64^(-m)>=exp(-540x^2).

For the dyadic Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady flow Phi of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential with X i.i.d. uniform and any fixed L>0, each coordinate k, each alpha in (2,infinity] and each M, with probability tending to one int psi_alpha(4|Phi_k(x)|/(L sqrt(N log N))) dx >= M (psi_alpha(u)=e^(u^alpha)-1, psi_infinity(u)=N(u-1)_+). So the flow-bound value of this flow, for any lambda' within a constant factor of N, exceeds every multiple of N at every pair with an exponent above 2, in particular at every pair of the ultimate matching curve.

For alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2<1/2 and every fixed L>0, for X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y either evenly spread or an independent uniform sample, with probability tending to one no matching satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N (maximum bound L sqrt(log N/N) at infinity) for both j=1,2. So the ultimate matching conjecture cannot be strengthened below its curve at any pair, in either setting; e.g. (alpha,infinity) fails for every alpha>2.

For X={1..n}, Y=X+h on the line (h=floor(sqrt n), n>=4), nested graphs G_k={|x-y|<=e^(k-1)} for k from any k_0<=1 (or all integers) up to complete, weights w_k=e^k and m_k the deficiency of G_k: sum_k w_k m_k <= e^2 h^2/(e-1)+e h/(e-1) while every perfect matching M has sum_k w_k |M minus G_k| >= n(h-1). So per-level Hall deficiencies cannot be glued into one matching at any constant factor.

Simulation, N=16*4^J uniform points, J=6..10, eight seeds each: the dyadic flow plus a greedy circulation per square (curl of a pyramid, chosen to minimize the quartic cost of the running field) has per-point kurtosis, after division by the dyadic flow's analytic per-position standard deviation, 2.71-2.89 against 2.88-3.19 for the dyadic flow, lower at every size with no trend in J, and moves variance from the first coordinate to the second (mean ratios 0.70-0.76 and 1.16-1.24).

For N >= N_0 and a rectangle Q=[0,a]x[0,b] with 1 <= a/b <= (log N)^(1/2) there is a fixed N-point set Z in Q, whose cells tile Q with area ab/N and diameter at most K sqrt(ab/N), such that for X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on Q, with probability at least 1-2(log N)^(1/2) N^(-2)-L (log N)^(1/2) exp(-(log N)^(3/2)/(3L)), some matching moves each coordinate by at most K sqrt(ab/N)(log N)^(3/4), K and L universal.

For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity], u_j=(log N)^(1/alpha_j), X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread or an independent uniform sample: if 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, with probability tending to one some matching has max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= K u_j sqrt(log N/N) for j=1,2, K universal; if 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 < 1/2, for every K this fails with probability tending to one. So the maximum-displacement consequence of the ultimate matching conjecture holds exactly on and above its curve.

If a matching is (L,alpha)-good in coordinate j with alpha in (0,infinity), then for every t>=0 at most 2N e^(-t) pairs have |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| >= L sqrt(log N/N) t^(1/alpha); hence for every a,delta,beta>0, if more than N (log N)^(-a) pairs have |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| >= delta (log N)^(1/2+beta)/sqrt N, the matching is not (L,alpha)-good in coordinate j for N >= N_0(a,delta,beta,L,alpha).

For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity], square cells of side s=s_N -> 0 with s sqrt N >= delta (log N)^(1/2+gamma) (delta,gamma>0 fixed), X,Y independent uniform samples: for each fixed measurable rule that, in each cell with excess z(u)>0, chooses z(u) of its X points by cell memberships and labels only and matches them to Y points outside the cell, and every L, with probability tending to one the matching fails to be (L,alpha_j)-good in some coordinate j. In particular the matching of [C5] (Ouimet, solution of Talagrand's Problem 5.3) fails the (4,4) condition for every L.

There is a universal L such that for alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, X,Y independent uniform samples of size N in [0,1]^2 and any sequence t=t_N in [1,log N], with probability tending to one some matching (depending on t) has at most 2N e^(-t) pairs with |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| > L sqrt(log N/N) t^(1/alpha_j) for some j; the failure probability tends to zero uniformly in t. So each level of the ultimate matching condition common to both coordinates holds alone on and above the curve; a refutation must use mixed levels or levels coupled in one matching.

For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity] (no curve condition), every L>0, X,Y independent uniform samples of size N in [0,1]^2 and levels t_1,t_2 in [1,log N] with t_1^(1/alpha_1)/t_2^(1/alpha_2) -> infinity and e^(2 t_2) <= (L^2/8) log N t_1^(1/alpha_1) t_2^(1/alpha_2), with probability tending to one some matching has |X_i^1-Y^1_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N/N) t_1^(1/alpha_1) for every i and at most 2N e^(-t_2) pairs with |X_i^2-Y^2_pi(i)| > L sqrt(log N/N) t_2^(1/alpha_2). At (4,4) with t_1=log N it covers t_2 <= (5/8) log log N + (1/8) log t_2 + O(1).

(1) For convex phi_1,phi_2:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity] with phi_j(0)=0, Phi(G)=int sum_j phi_j(|d_j G|) on [0,1]^2 and Lipschitz G_1..G_m: sum_k Phi(G_k) <= Phi(sum G_k) + sigma, sigma the members' penalty on the set where their d_j G_k disagree in sign; if aligned (sigma=0), l(sum G_k) <= Phi(sum G_k) max_k l(G_k)^+/Phi(G_k) for any linear l. (2) For phi_j=psi*_alpha_j, alpha_j in [1,infinity) and theta, C>0 fixed, m <= (log N)^C, nonzero gradient components >= N^theta and Phi(sum G_k) <= 2: l(sum G_k) <= (1+sigma/2)(1+c_0 log log N/log N) max_k l(H_k)^+, H_k = G_k rescaled to Phi(H_k)=2, l vanishing on constants.

(1) For band functions G_k(x,y)=A_k min{1,max{0,(f_k(x)+w-y)/w}} on [0,1]^2 over continuous piecewise linear graphs f_k, k<=m, with every difference f_k-f_k' having at most P linear pieces, and convex phi_1 with phi_1(y)<=rho y for y<=Y, A_k|f_k'|<=wY: the vertical gradients are aligned and the members' penalty on the misaligned set is sigma <= 2 rho w P (m-1) sum_k A_k. (2) For scaled Leighton-Shor graphs kappa_k F_k (F_k of the form (4.122) of Talagrand's monograph, kappa_k in [(log N)^(-1/2),(log N)^(1/2)], A_k<=1, w the grid side, phi_j=psi*_alpha_j finite): sigma <= (L/4) m^2 (log N)^(3/2) N^(-1/2+1/100). (3) Hence, for positively oriented members with m<=(log N)^C and Phi(sum G_k)<=2: l(sum G_k) <= (1+sigma/2)(1+c_0 log log N/log N) max_k l(H_k)^+, H_k rescaled to Phi(H_k)=2, with no additive term.

In the setting of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction (X i.i.d. uniform, Y evenly spread, L>=132, cell-smeared measures on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N)), there is a universal L_0 such that for every L>=132, with probability tending to one the penalized discrepancy D_N is at least sqrt(N log N)/(4 L_0) for all alpha_1,alpha_2 in [1,infinity] simultaneously, endpoints included; more generally on the same event for every class of Lipschitz functions containing the 1-Lipschitz functions vanishing on the boundary (any separable penalty with nondecreasing phi_j, phi_j(1) <= 1).

(1) For N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2, a grid of square cells of side delta, cell-uniform smearings mu_X, mu_Y, a bijection pi with D_i the difference of the centres of the cells of Y_pi(i) and X_i, tube density rho_pi(x) = delta^(-2) sum_i Leb{t in [0,1]: x - t D_i in Q(X_i)}, convex phi_j with phi_j(0)=0 and conjugates phi_j*, every Lipschitz G and lambda>0: int G d(mu_X - mu_Y) <= lambda sum_j [sum_i phi_j(|D_i^j|/lambda) + int phi_j*(|d_j G|) rho_pi dx]. (2) With alpha_j in [1,infinity], phi_j = psi_alpha_j, delta <= s, sum_i psi_alpha_j(|X_i^j - Y^j_pi(i)|/s) <= N for j=1,2 and rho_pi <= K N: every Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) <= 2 has int G d(mu_X - mu_Y) <= 2(e+2K) s N.

In the setting of lem:tube-density-converse (cells of side delta, cell-uniform smearings, bijection pi, centre differences D_i, tube densities rho_i with rho_pi = sum rho_i): the segment flux Phi_pi = sum_i D_i rho_i is a bounded flow from mu_X to mu_Y (int grad g . Phi_pi = int g d(mu_Y - mu_X) for Lipschitz g), and for convex psi_j >= 0 with psi_j(0)=0, lambda > 0 and M >= max rho_pi: sum_j int M psi_j(|Phi_pi,j|/(lambda M)) dx <= sum_j sum_i psi_j(|D_i^j|/lambda). So for the flow bound's fixed density level lambda', the flow -Phi_pi has cost lambda' int C_mu(-Phi_pi/lambda') <= (lambda'/M) 2N at the cost scale mu = lambda M/lambda' when the matching's cost is at most 2N.

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and l_1 the Leighton-Shor scale (2^(-l_1) >= (log N)^(3/4)/sqrt N), with probability tending to one, for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1: (a) every closed simple curve C traced on the grid of mesh 2^(-j) has |sum_i (1_{int C}(X_i) - lambda(int C))| <= L sqrt N l(C) ((log_2(2^(j+3) l(C)))^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)); (b) every H constant on the cells has |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(H), V_j the cell variation (inner jumps times 2^(-j), plus the boundary ring against the best constant). (c) V_j(H) <= 4 times its inner variation (median constant; boundary ring at most three times the inner boundary). For Lipschitz G its cell averages have V_j at most 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|).

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one, for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale) and every bounded G Lipschitz on each open cell of mesh 2^(-j): |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(E_j G) + L sqrt(N log N) Lambda_j(G), E_j G the cell averages, V_j their cell variation, Lambda_j(G) the sum over cells Q of Lip(G on Q) times area(Q); for Lipschitz G, V_j(E_j G) <= 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|). Corollary at (4,4), against Lebesgue measure: if int sum psi*_4(|d_i G|) <= 2 and each |d_i G| is 0 or in [y, 2y] with e^16 <= y <= 2^(l_1), then for every j <= j* = min(l_1, floor((log N)^(2/3)(log y)^(1/3))) the discrepancy is at most L sqrt(N log N)(1 + y area(U_j)), U_j the cells on which G is not constant; so L(1+K) sqrt(N log N) when area(U_j) <= K area(supp grad G).

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one, for all 1 <= j_1 <= j_2 <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale), every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides between 2^(-j_2) and 2^(-j_1), every H constant on its cells and every c: |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N ((j_1^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V^c(H) + (j_2^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V^c_f(H)), V^c the cell variation (jumps times edge lengths, boundary edges against c) and V^c_f its part over fine edges (partition edges that are not whole edges of the mesh 2^(-j_1)). For a closed simple curve on the partition's edges, the bound is L sqrt N ((j_1^(3/4)+sqrt(log N)) l(C) + (j_2^(3/4)+sqrt(log N)) l_f(C)).

With probability tending to one and a universal L: in lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (a) the factor becomes (log_2(2^(j+3) l(C)))^(3/4) + sqrt(j + log log N); in its (b) and in lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy the term sqrt(log N) beside j^(3/4) (beside j_1^(3/4), j_2^(3/4)) becomes sqrt(j + log log N) (sqrt(j_1 + log log N), sqrt(j_2 + log log N)), so those factors are at most 2 j^(3/4) + sqrt(log log N). The failure probability is of order (log N)^(-c L^2), weaker than the earlier forms'; both events can be intersected.

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and F(i) = i^(3/4) + (2 + log_2 i) sqrt(log log N) (at most i^(3/4) + C (log log N)^(3/2)), with probability tending to one: (a) for every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides 2^(-i), 1 <= i <= l_1 (the Leighton-Shor scale), and every H constant on its cells, |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N sum over inner edges e of length(e) |jump_e H| F(i(e)), i(e) the level of the smaller cell beside e; (b) for every such partition in which neighbouring cells differ in side by a factor at most 2, and every Lipschitz G, |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L sqrt N sum_Q F(i(Q)) int_Q (|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|) + L sqrt(N log N) sum_Q Lip(G on Q) area(Q). In (b) G may be Lipschitz on each cell only, its jumps across edges added at their edges' factors.

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one: for every y >= e^16, every j <= j*(y) = min(l_1, floor((log N)^(2/3)(log y)^(1/3))), and every Lipschitz G with int sum psi*_4(|d_i G|) <= 2 whose larger partial is at least y where grad G is nonzero, |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L' sqrt(N log N)(1 + Lambda_j(G)) with L' universal, Lambda_j the sum over cells of mesh 2^(-j) of Lip(G on Q) area(Q). The same holds with the cellwise sum over any balanced dyadic partition with cells of level at most j*(y). The witness of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound at (4,4), built with the reduction's parameter L >= 132, has Lambda_(l_1) <= 297/L, so the bound is of the conjectured order on it, against Lebesgue measure.

On the event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, for 0 <= k <= j <= l_1, W = 2^(-k), Phi = (2(j-k)+5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N): (a) a union A of cells of mesh 2^(-j) has |sum_i 1_A(X_i) - N area(A)| <= L sqrt N Phi (perimeter(A) + 4W #{W-cells containing a cell of A}); (b) a cell function H has the bound with V^0(H) + 4W sum over W-cells of (max H^+ + max H^-); on the event of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation, (a) and (b) hold with sqrt(j + log log N) in Phi. (c) A band a phi(y - f(x)) with |f'| <= K, ramp width w >= 2^(-l_1) and band width W' <= 1 has discrepancy at most L(1+K)^2 a sqrt N((2 log_2(W'/w) + 9)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)). (d) Disjoint such bands inside the square at their own ramp gradients e^16 <= y_r <= N, B = sum of amplitudes: at most L(1+K)^2 sqrt N(sum_r a_r (2 log_2 y_r)^(3/4) + B(2 log_2(1+1/B) + 9)^(3/4) + B sqrt(log N)); under class cost at most 2 this is O((1+K)^2 sqrt(N log N)). (e) The plain per-cell count bound: a band with ramps w >= 6 sqrt(log N/N) has discrepancy at most L(1+K)^2 (1 + W'/w) a sqrt(N log N). Against Lebesgue measure.

For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, s_0 = 3 sqrt(log N/N), w_0 = 2 s_0, with probability tending to one: (a) for every mesh 2^(-i) >= s_0 and every set S of cells of mesh 2^(-(i-1)) meeting each column in an interval of at most K+4 cells, neighbouring intervals starting at most K+1 rows apart, the sum over the children Q of S of |n_Q - n_parent/4| is at most L((K+4) sqrt N + sqrt((K+4) N 2^(-i) log N)); (b) every band a phi(y - f(x)) with |f'| <= K, any ramp width w > 0 and band width W' <= 1 has discrepancy at most L(1+K)^2 a sqrt N((2 log_2(2 + W'/max(w,w_0)) + 9)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)); (c) disjoint bands inside the square along full-width graphs, slopes at most K, ramp gradients y_r >= e^16, any ramp widths, with class cost at most 2 have discrepancy at most L(1+K)^2 sqrt(N log N). Against Lebesgue measure.

On the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, with rho a bounded measurable mollifier supported in the unit disc and L depending only on its sup norm: for every 1 <= j <= l_1, h = 2^(-j), and every Lipschitz G on [0,1]^2, the mollification S of the even reflection of G at scale h has |sum_i S(X_i) - N int S| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) ||grad G||_1, its cellwise sum at mesh h being at most 81 ||rho||_inf ||grad G||_1. For class functions at (4,4) whose larger partial is at least y >= e^16 where the gradient is nonzero and j <= j*(y), this is O(sqrt(N log N)), so the single-level class bound reduces to the remainder G - S. Against Lebesgue measure.

For every exponent pair alpha in [1,infinity]^2 (beta = max_j 1/alpha_j), every N, every level y >= 2 (y <= N if an exponent is infinite) and every N points x_i in [0,1]^2: with r = (2Ny(log(1+y))^beta)^(-1/2), a = yr, G = max_i max(0, a - y|z - x_i|_inf) has cost int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) <= 2, one partial +-y and the other 0 a.e. where grad G != 0, and sum_i G(x_i) - N int G >= (2/3) N a = (sqrt 2/3) sqrt(N y) (log(1+y))^(-beta/2). So against Lebesgue measure the conjugate class is unbounded for every point set when both exponents are finite, and at least (sqrt 2/3) N (log(1+N))^(-beta/2) when one is infinite (cell smearing is necessary); at (4,4) a Lebesgue bound L' sqrt(N log N) for the functions of level at least y fails for every point set once (sqrt 2/3) sqrt y (log(1+y))^(-1/8) > L' sqrt(log N), e.g. y = (log N)^2.

On a finite set with a stochastic splitting rule P, irreducible and reversible with respect to pi (conductances c(x,y) = pi(x)p(x,y)), and initial mass eta and thresholds t with equal sums: every divisible-sandpile odometer v >= 0 whose final configuration eta - v + P^T v is at most t ends exactly at t, and its net flow v(x)p(x,y) - v(y)p(y,x) equals c(x,y)(u(x) - u(y)) for any solution of sum_y c(x,y)(u(x) - u(y)) = eta(x) - t(x): the same for every such stabilizing odometer, linear in eta - t, the electrical (least-energy) flow; odometers exist (v = pi (u - min u)). For a non-reversible rule the flow is unique only up to a circulation. With equal splitting on the grid of cells and uniform thresholds, the sandpile odometer flow is the electrical flow, and every balanced transport flow is it plus a divergence-free circulation.

(a) On a finite set with a stochastic splitting rule P, irreducible and reversible with respect to pi (conductances c(x,y) = pi(x)p(x,y)), the net flow of every finite sequence of divisible-sandpile stages with this one rule, whatever their thresholds and odometers (the proof uses neither thresholds, stability nor the sign of the odometers), carrying eta to eta', is the electrical flow from eta to eta' with conductances c; in particular the slack sandpile with thresholds (1+eps) times the background followed by the balanced sandpile to the background has exactly the electrical flow, for every eps >= 0 and every sample. (b) The deficit-first divisible sandpile (scan in index order; a site above its threshold sends its excess to the neighbours below theirs in proportion to their deficits, fills them and splits any rest equally among all neighbours, or splits equally when none is below) has a net flow that is not additive in the excess: on the cycle of four cells with thresholds 0, F((2,0,-1,-1)) + F((-1,-1,2,0)) = (0,-1,0,-1) on the edges 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-1 while F((1,-1,1,-1)) = (1/2,-1/2,1/2,-1/2). (c) For N i.i.d. uniform points and M square cells of mean count mu = N delta^2, with probability at least 1 - M exp(-mu h(eps)), h(eps) = (1+eps) log(1+eps) - eps, no cell holds more than (1+eps) mu points; on the reduction's grid this holds with probability tending to one for every fixed eps with h(eps) > 1089/L^2.
